propositions: Plan-review grounding finders (G1G2/E4/E6) check only the origin/main snapshot and ignore prerequisite tickets, causing symbols that a depends_on ticket will create to be flagged as missing/unverifiable even though the prose rule states such symbols should be treated as existing.

A plan citing a symbol with [rebar:<id>] notation should have that citation verified via bidirectional dependency edges (either the plan depends_on the cited ticket, or the cited ticket blocks the plan) before grounding decisions are made.
The citation verification (Layer 1) must be advisory and never block; it reuses det_operator_attested's parsing approach and fail-open architecture without adding a new floor-level blocking check.

The LLM grounding finders (Layer 2) must use show_ticket to retrieve cited prerequisites and affirmatively confirm coverage of the specific missing functionality before crediting the citation; uncited, edge-unbacked, or coverage-unconfirmed citations result in findings standing.
Reverse-lookup failures (network, missing ticket, store errors) must be caught and treated as unverified citations, never propagating exceptions into the advisory lane.
The implementation must reside in a separate det_citation.py module (not inline in det_floor.py) due to module-size policy constraints.
